top.text: A thousand games, respect. One trick that helps: sort the pile by how long each game takes to finish and clear the short ones first, so the number drops fast.
Smart to be careful before the first account. Once you have it, wishlist whatever catches your eye: Steam tells you when something on it goes on sale, so there's no pressure to buy on impulse.

Access years from now is the one that price can't fix later. DRM-free games, like the ones on GOG, cover a lot of it: you keep the installer, it plays offline, and it doesn't depend on a launcher or an account.
Driver update first, then cap the frame rate a few fps below your monitor's refresh rate. That alone smooths out a lot of stutter.
Ugh, 50GB hiding out of sight is frustrating. The Storage page in the Deck settings shows what's taking up space, which is a good first stop when something doesn't add up.
